Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`), estVoice (s: the predicted voice length, tools/estimate.py; replaced by the real voice once tools/voice.py has run).

source: THE FULL-EPIC TRAILER, second cut (pipeline number 97; never a numbered episode). Every shot is a line. Every beat was read in the constituted text of the BORI Critical Edition (GRETIL e-text, lab/ce/): the verses, a Sanskrit quotation for each and everything cut or reworded are in script/TRAILER-CHECK.md; the edit is planned shot by shot in script/TRAILER-EDIT.md. In short: 6.23.21-47 and 6.24.9 (the chariot between the armies; the bow let go; 'I will not fight'), 1.94.86-90, 1.104.10-15 and 3.292.6-7, 1.107.1, 1.132.8-12 and 1.136.4-10, 1.139.1-4 and 1.142.28-31, 1.155.41, 2.42.21-25, 2.53-54 and 2.58.29-37, 2.61.40-41 (the cloth: no cause is named; Krishna is not shown), 2.67.9-10 and 2.68.1 (deerskins), 5.125.26, 6.114.81-85, 7.33.12 and 7.48.13, 8.66.60-65 and 8.67.24, 10.8.9-11, 11.25.36-42, 17.1.23-31 and 17.3.7-8, 6.33.3-35 (the universal form; 'I am Time' is 6.33.32 kalo 'smi), 1.1.52 (itihasa). 'Iti-ha-asa: so indeed it was' is the traditional analysis of the word, not a verse.
structure: TITLE (music, the name, no voice) -> NOW: the chariot between two armies, an archer who will not fight -> THE PAST in order, in the present tense, cut three times by a wordless return to the chariot, each closer -> STOP 1 -> the conch: past and battlefield meet at 'Two armies' -> WHAT WILL COME, in the future tense, the fastest cutting of the film -> 'But first': the universal form, the one long hold -> STOP 2, the clock dead on 'I am Time' -> the word itihasa -> the promise -> the hard cut to the end card on the last word.

names.Karna: born in armour, a charioteer's foster-son

loop.hookQuestion: Why will the archer not fight, and what does he see?

strings.sourceLine: Text: the Mahabharata · BORI Critical Edition

lines.note: OPENING, no voice: the war drums, a low drone, the conch, a rising swell; from high above, two armies as dark masses under a red dawn, banners moving, the camera coming down; MAHABHARATA arrives large, legible by 1.5 s.

lines.text: Two armies wait. Between them, one archer will not fight.
lines.note: NOW (CE 6.23.21, 6.23.47, 6.24.9): a tilt down the banner to one chariot standing between the two armies; Arjuna's bow is sinking, Krishna (seen from behind, dark) turns to him. Plaque: Arjuna.

lines.text: Long before, a prince swears away his throne and his line.
lines.note: CE 1.94.86-90: a slow push-in on the young prince's face as he raises his hand before the fisher-king; flowers begin to fall. Plaque: Bhishma.

lines.text: A mother gives her first-born to the river.
lines.note: CE 1.104.10-15, 3.292.6-7: the basket with the shining child, close; the camera pulls back and the river takes it: wide water, the girl small on the bank. Plaque: Karna.
INSERT 1 (wordless, one low conch note): the chariot between the armies, WIDE. The same blue-iron light every time.

lines.text: A hundred brothers. Five cousins. One throne.
lines.note: CE 1.107.1: Duryodhana large in the foreground; the focus racks to the five across the hall, then to the one seat. Plaque: Duryodhana.
CE 1.132.8-12, 1.136.4-10: the lacquered house in flames; a tilt down through the earth to six figures leaving by a tunnel with one lamp (larger than in the first cut).
CE 1.139.1-4, 1.142.28-31: the rakshasa reaches; Bhima's blow lands and the shot is CUT three frames after the contact.
INSERT 2 (wordless, the same conch note): closer: the two figures on the chariot, Arjuna and the dark shape of Krishna.

lines.text: A woman rises from a fire-altar.
lines.note: CE 1.155.41: Draupadi rises out of the middle of the altar; the camera rises with her. Plaque: Draupadi.
CE 2.42.21-25: Krishna from behind and in profile, a dark shape lit only by the wheel; it leaves his hand and the camera goes with it. His lit face is withheld. Plaque: Krishna.
CE 2.53-54: the dice rattle before the picture; a push-in on Yudhishthira's face as he decides. Plaque: Yudhishthira.
CE 2.58: from above: the dice fall, strike the red cloth; CUT three frames after they land.
CE 2.58.29-37: the stakes swept across the cloth to Shakuni's side: five crowns, then a red veil.
CE 2.61.40: close: a hand hauls the red cloth across the frame; her figure holds still.
CE 2.61.41: the pull-back: the hall of seated kings around her, heads bowed, and the cloth running out of frame and heaped on the floor. No cause is shown; Krishna is not there.
INSERT 3 (wordless, the same conch note): closest: Arjuna's hand opening on the bow.
CE 2.67.9-10, 2.68.1: six figures walk away under great trees, deerskins over their shoulders (ajinany uttariyani).
CE 5.125.26: the court; the envoy a dark back in the foreground; the focus goes to the king on his seat.
THE CLOSE-UP (CE 5.125.26): a push-in on Duryodhana's face. STOP 1: on the frame after 'earth' every sound cuts to nothing; the push, the lamp and the embers go on.
THE TURN (CE 6.23.21): the conch six frames before the cut; the wide of the inserts, now held: both armies, the chariot between them.
CE 6.23.47: a slow push-in on Arjuna as he sits and the bow leaves his hand.
CE 6.114.81: the arrows are heard before the picture; close: arrows streak left to right past his face as he goes back.
CE 6.114.84-85: the pull-back: he lies on the arrows and does not touch the ground; the field at sunset.
CE 7.33.12: close on Abhimanyu, sword up.
CE 7.48.13 (eko bahubhih): wide: the ring of spears and wheels closes from both sides. The blow is not shown.
CE 8.66.60-64: Karna on his knees, heaving at the wheel; the red sun behind him.
CE 8.66.60, 8.67.24: the wheel drops into the earth; CUT three frames after it stops, the hub on the rhyme spot.

lines.text: A camp raided in its sleep.
lines.note: CE 10.8.9-11: night; dark tents; one man with a blade goes in, left to right, not by the gate.

lines.text: A mother of a hundred sons will curse Krishna.
lines.note: CE 11.25.36-42: Gandhari, blindfolded, her hand rising toward a dark figure with his back to us; a field of fires behind.

lines.text: And at the end, a king will not abandon his dog.
lines.note: CE 17.1.23-31, 17.3.7: snow and the mountain; the old king walking up, the dog at his heel; he stops and turns to it. The quietest shot: the clock, the wind and the voice.

lines.text: But first, Arjuna asks to see. Krishna shows him everything. “I am Time.”
lines.note: THE SIGNATURE SHOT AND THE ONE LONG HOLD (CE 6.33.3-35; every drawn element is cited in TRAILER-CHECK.md): tight on Arjuna's face; the light of a thousand suns comes up on it; the camera pulls back and up until he is a speck with joined palms under a form with many faces, eyes and arms that leaves the frame on every side, warriors streaming into its mouths. STOP 2: after 'I am Time' every sound cuts dead, the clock with it; the form goes on turning.

lines.text: It calls itself itihasa. Iti. Ha. Asa. So indeed it was.
lines.note: After the full stop (CE 1.1.52): dark, embers; the word in gold; it opens into its three parts as each is said, each with its gloss; then the meaning. One struck note under 'was'.
THE PROMISE: the names of the eighteen books run up the frame in gold.
The raised hand of the vow again, closer.
The line of spears again, sliding.

lines.text: From the first verse to the last.
lines.note: The Naimisha fire at the blue hour; the storyteller comes to it.

lines.text: Nothing added for effect. Follow. Episode
lines.note: First light: Vyasa by the great fire, a hand opening to us. FOLLOW arrives on its word.

The last word lands on a hard cut to the end card and one struck note: the source line, Episode 1 · The Storyteller Arrives, FOLLOW. Embers and a slow pull keep it alive; the note rings and is not faded under a wash.
